articles.title: Why Standard PDF Taggers Turn LaTeX Matrices Into Gibberish (and 4 Math TTS Traps)
articles.excerpt: With ADA Title II (WCAG 2.1 AA) deadlines coming up for U.S. public universities, most accessibility discussions focus on web pages and body text. In math, physics, and engineering departments, the re…
articles.body: With ADA Title II (WCAG 2.1 AA) deadlines coming up for U.S. public universities, most accessibility discussions focus on web pages and body text. In math, physics, and engineering departments, the real bottleneck is legacy lecture PDFs: compiled LaTeX where the .tex source is long gone, old Word/MathType exams, and scanned handwritten notes. Even when a campus runs standard PDF auto-taggers over those handouts, the output often looks fine visually while completely breaking for screen-reader users. Here are the failure modes we kept hitting while building EqScribe and testing real open STEM courseware (OpenStax CC BY 4.0 chapters, multivariable calculus handouts, and a 0-text-layer 1903 handwritten page from Srinivasa Ramanujan's notebook). 1.

articles.title: Back up MongoDB to S3: from mongodump to a verified restore
articles.excerpt: Most MongoDB backup guides stop at the mongodump command line. That is the This guide covers the whole chain. By the end you will know what a mongodump --oplog is worth anything, how to mongosh tell y…
articles.body: Most MongoDB backup guides stop at the mongodump command line. That is the easy part. What decides whether you get your data back is everything around it: what the dump leaves out, which options change what you will be able to restore, whether the script really fails when the dump fails, and whether anyone has ever replayed the file. This guide covers the whole chain. By the end you will know what a mongodump holds and what it leaves to the server, when --oplog is worth anything, how to write a backup script that cannot report success on an empty file, how to restore the archive by hand in a throwaway container, and which questions asked in mongosh tell you a restored database actually holds your data. Everything here works with mongodump , docker and the AWS CLI, and nothing else.

articles.body: For two years, the honest advice about cheap AI models has been cautious: audit your tiers, pilot the budget lane, see what sticks. This month, the evidence changed shape. In OpenAI's own launch data for GPT-6.2, the cheap model in the lineup — Sol — scored 73.0% on Agents' Last Exam v1.1 at $1.32 per task. Claude Fable 5.2, running the same benchmark at max effort, scored 72.8% at $60.05 per task. The cheaper model didn't just keep up. It scored a hair higher at roughly one forty-fifth of the price. The Tie That Should Change Your Budget One benchmark tie can be a fluke. Two is a pattern. On Artificial Analysis's AA-3D, human judges look at two anonymous interactive 3D experiences built from the same prompt and vote for the one they prefer.

articles.title: Exporting SVG, DXF, PDF and EPS in the browser with no libraries
articles.excerpt: Free Christmas SVG is a library of free cut files for Cricut and Silhouette machines: snowflakes, trees, Santa hats, sayings. Every design has a small editor on its page. You can recolour it, resize i…
articles.body: Free Christmas SVG is a library of free cut files for Cricut and Silhouette machines: snowflakes, trees, Santa hats, sayings. Every design has a small editor on its page. You can recolour it, resize it, rotate or mirror it, add an offset border, and then download it as SVG, DXF, PDF, EPS, PNG, JPG or WebP. There's no server involved, and no export library either. The site's runtime dependencies are Astro, Tailwind, a sitemap plugin and fonts. Every file writer is hand-written, in one 267-line file. The editor script is 13 KB gzipped. That's only possible because of a decision made long before the editor existed: every design is made of straight lines. Key takeaways Constrain your source data, and the format writers become simple.

articles.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
articles.excerpt: Colorful metaphors, a near-miss with Eddie Murphy and humpback whales in 20th-century California.
articles.body: It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters.
